rule: Code outside a method body: the caller is its location. Field/val initializer → `Type#field`; ... Non-lazy initializers also get an `implicit` edge from `<clinit>`/`<init>`; lazy ones do not. ... Companion-object members flatten onto the class.
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type or object name) is method; a class-name call `T(..)` that resolves to a constructor, and `: this(..)` / `: super(..)` / a supertype-list call, are constructor. Kotlin has no `new`; a `val x = T(..)` constructor call is treated as decision A's `= new T(...)`. Property initializers are `Type#prop` callers with an implicit edge from <init> (instance) at the property's line. The `init {}` block runs as part of the primary constructor, so its caller is Settings#<init> (its location). `private val size: Int` has no initializer: no edge. The companion `val DEFAULT = create()` flattens to Settings#DEFAULT; on the JVM a companion property is a static field of the outer class, initialized in the outer class's static initializer, so the implicit edge comes from Settings#<clinit>. SPEC gives no confidence for implicit edges; high because both ends are in the scanned source. `java.util.ArrayList` is qualified through its explicit import (type argument dropped), medium. `loader` is typed Loader by its `= Loader(path)` initializer. `Loader.warm()` names the companion member, flattened to Loader#warm.
